title: Schizophrenia - BSV and Vocal Features
content:
DOCUMENT TYPE: BSV / Vocal

BSV / VOCAL SIGNALS: Disorganized speech produces high Arousal with erratic pitch, rate, and volume. Negative symptoms: Low Arousal, low Valence, low Dominance (flat affect, alogia, avolition). Voice often monotone, soft, with long pauses, reduced pitch range, and impoverished prosody. Delusional content may produce sudden high-arousal spikes when discussing fixed false beliefs.

PATIENT-LANGUAGE EXAMPLES: "The voices tell me things no one else hears", "I feel nothing most days", "My thoughts get jumbled when I try to explain".

COUNTER-SIGNALS / NEGATIONS: Normal fluent prosody, consistent affect, no reports of hallucinations or fixed delusions.

PROVENANCE: Clinical observation and computational linguistics research on thought disorder and negative symptoms.
